outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms will spread across parts of the Northeast and Ohio Valley Thursday afternoon/evening. Large hail, damaging winds, and a few tornadoes can be expected. Strong/severe thunderstorms with hail/wind will also develop across portions of the central Plains into the lower Missouri Valley region. Isolated strong storms will also develop across the lower Mississippi Valley.

sections.title: Northeast/Ohio Valley
sections.text: Upper ridge currently positioned over the southern Appalachians will build west as a pronounced short-wave trough progresses across the Great Lakes during the day. This feature will suppress the height field as far south as the northern middle Atlantic as 500mb speed max approaches the base of the trough across upstate NY late in the period. Latest model guidance suggests strong boundary layer heating will occur across the upper OH Valley ahead of a pre frontal trough. This should allow for rapid and seasonally strong destabilization from portions of eastern OH across western PA into portions of western NY. Early-day convection that forms along a north-south corridor of warm advection will suppress destabilization downstream and the primary concern for robust thunderstorm development will be within the zone of strong surface heating. Pattern evolution will lead to deepening westerly flow that will encourage steep lapse rates to be resupplied into the upper OH Valley. Forecast soundings prior to convective initiation exhibit SBCAPE in excess of 3000 J/kg with surface-6km bulk shear greater than 40kt across portions of the ENH Risk. sections.title: Central Plains to Lower MO Valley
sections.text: Surface front is forecast to stall across the middle of the country and extend roughly across northern MO/KS into northeast CO. While large-scale support aloft will be minimized as upper ridging shifts into this part of the US, low-level warm advection will prove instrumental in a corridor of convection, particularly during the latter half of the period. Strong daytime heating will remove inhibition near the front and this will contribute to strong buoyancy across northern KS into the lower MO River Valley. Latest guidance suggests robust convection should evolve over southeast NE then spread/propagate southeast during the evening. An MCS may ultimately evolve along the cool side of the front and this cluster should spread toward the lower OH Valley late in the period. Hail/wind are the primary risks.

sections.title: Lower MS Valley
sections.text: Notable easterly wave has contributed to a pronounced cluster of strong/severe thunderstorms across portions of GA into AL late this evening. This feature is expected to once again contribute to scattered robust convection during the day as boundary layer warming destabilizes the air mass. Gusty winds/hail may be noted with the strongest convection across the lower MS Valley. ..Darrow/Squitieri.. 06/16/2022

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms will spread across parts of the Northeast and Ohio Valley Thursday afternoon/evening. Large hail, damaging winds, and a few tornadoes can be expected. Strong/severe thunderstorms with hail/wind will also develop across portions of the central Plains into the lower Missouri Valley region. Isolated strong storms will also develop across the Gulf Coast states.

sections.title: Northeast States
sections.text: Morning water vapor imagery shows an upper ridge extending from TN into New England. This ridge will rapidly shift eastward today as a progressive upper low over northwest Ontario approaches, resulting in large scale forcing and strengthening winds aloft overspreading the Northeast states. A very moist and potentially unstable air mass is present over much of NY/PA, where daytime highs well into the 80s and dewpoints near 70F will yield MLCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg and little capping inversion. Present indications are that thunderstorms will form along an approaching cold front over northeast OH into western NY, while other isolated cells intensify in the warm sector across parts of NY/PA. Low-level winds are not forecast to be particularly strong, but favorable deep-layer shear and degree of instability suggest that discrete supercells will be possible, capable of very large hail and a few tornadoes. This activity will spread eastward during the afternoon/evening across the ENH risk area, with upscale growth into short bowing segments expected. Damaging winds and hail would be the primary threats.

sections.title: MO/IL Vicinity
sections.text: As the aforementioned upper low shifts eastward into the Great Lakes region, a cold front will sag southward into the mid MS and OH valleys. Weak forcing aloft is expected to limit convective development during the day. However, a strengthening low-level jet will likely contribute to scattered thunderstorms by mid-evening along and just north of the front. This activity will build southeastward through the evening with a large hail and damaging wind threat.

sections.title: Gulf Coast States
sections.text: Similar to yesterday, westward-moving afternoon thunderstorms are expected from the FL Panhandle westward into parts of LA/MS. Hot and humid conditions with temperatures in the mid/upper 90s and large CAPE values will promote damaging wind gusts in the stronger cores. ..Hart/Mosier.. 06/16/2022

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected across parts of the Northeast and Ohio Valley this afternoon/evening. Large hail, damaging winds, and possibly a few tornadoes can be expected. Strong/severe thunderstorms with hail/wind will also develop across portions of the central Plains into the lower Missouri Valley region. Isolated strong storms will also develop across the Gulf Coast states.

sections.title: Northeast/Mid-Atlantic States
sections.text: An active severe-weather day is expected across the region, with essentially all convective modes/hazards possible. Steady large-scale height falls, along with a strengthening of cyclonically curved westerlies, will occur via the approach of the upstream trough over Ontario. Upstream regional 12z soundings/upper-air data sampled 50+ kt mid-level winds early this morning over Lower Michigan into Illinois (and likely Indiana). A very moist and potentially unstable air mass is in place across the Northeast, where daytime highs well into the 80s F and dewpoints near 70F will yield MLCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg with little capping inversion. General thinking remains that thunderstorms will form this afternoon along an approaching cold front, initially from western/northern New York into northwest Pennsylvania into eastern/central Ohio, with additional development possible within the warm sector in vicinity of the mountains and/or lee trough. Low-level winds are not forecast to be particularly strong, but favorable deep-layer shear and degree of instability suggest that discrete supercells will be possible, capable of very large hail and possibly a few tornadoes. sections.title: Central Appalachians/Carolinas
sections.text: On the eastern periphery of the Tennessee Valley-centered upper ridge, mid-level temperatures have cooled since yesterday, by as much as 1-2.5C at 700 mb over the past 24 hours as per 12z observed soundings from KRNK/KGSO. This should result in a more active day for thunderstorms across the region including the potential for pulse-type downbursts capable of localized wind damage. A gradual clustering/modest organization of storms could occur, pending sufficient storm development, aided by a modestly enhanced belt of northwesterly mid-level winds, which are noted on the northeast periphery of the upper ridge. Several convection-allowing models (such as NSSL-ARW and NAM 3km) lend credence to this possibility.

sections.title: Parts of Nebraska/Kansas into Missouri/Illinois
sections.text: A cold front will sag southward across the Midwest, while the front remains quasi-stationary from western/northern Kansas into northern Missouri. A northward-building upper ridge (centered over the Mid-South) will influence additional capping and likely limit deep convective development during the day. The most likely scenario is for storms to develop/increase this evening into the overnight along/north of the boundary as the low-level jet strengthens. Large hail would be the main threat initially, but damaging wind potential may also emerge, particularly as storm mergers occur and storms tend to grow upscale.

sections.title: Gulf Coast States
sections.text: Although probably not as widespread as across Alabama/Georgia late yesterday afternoon into evening, west/southwest-moving afternoon and early evening thunderstorms are again expected from the Florida Panhandle westward into parts of Mississippi/Louisiana. Hot and humid conditions with temperatures in the mid/upper 90s and large CAPE values will promote damaging wind gusts in the stronger cores. ..Guyer/Lyons.. 06/16/2022

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms will continue across parts of the Northeast and Ohio Valley this afternoon/evening. Large hail, damaging winds, and possibly a few tornadoes can be expected. Strong/severe thunderstorms with hail/wind will also develop across portions of the central Plains into the lower Missouri Valley region. Isolated strong storms will also continue across the Gulf Coast states.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Only minor line adjustments appear necessary with this outlook update, as severe storms continue to evolve as expected from the Lake Ontario vicinity to central Ohio on western fringes of the ENH outlook, from central Maryland to northwestern Georgia through the southern extension of the SLGT risk, and across portions of the central Gulf Coast area/lower Mississippi Valley within the MRGL risk area. Meanwhile, storm development remains likely across the Mid Missouri Valley area, and then spreading east-southeastward across the Lower Missouri Valley this evening/overnight. ..Goss.. 06/16/2022 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1141 AM CDT Thu Jun 16 2022/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated to widely scattered storm development may occur quickly early this afternoon ahead of advancing mid-level trough. Strong to severe storms may pose a risk for damaging wind gusts and hail through the afternoon. Storm coverage remains uncertain but A weather watch is being considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As of 1645 UTC, ascent from a prominent eastward moving mid-level trough was visible on regional WV imagery across portions of the western Great Lakes and southern Canada. A band of agitated cumulus was noted along and east of a weak cold front across portions of northwestern OH. As further ascent from the approaching trough overspreads an already warm and moist boundary layer (surface temps in the upper 80s F) convective initiation appears likely as early as 18z. 50-60 kt mid-level westerly flow along the base of the trough is support strong but mostly unidirectional wind profiles. Area VADS show bulk shear values of 35-45 kt favorable for storm organization into short bowing segments and possibly supercells. With 1500-2500 J/kg of MLCAPE and little remaining inhibition, strong to severe storms may develop relatively quickly and pose a risk for damaging wind gusts and hail through this afternoon. The greatest coverage of organized storms, especially with severe hail potential, appears to be across the eastern most portions of OH into far western PA. Here, locally stronger flow aloft and near the surface may support a greater concentration of severe storms into the afternoon. While some uncertainty with storm coverage exists farther west, the overall parameter space does suggest an increasing severe threat from central OH eastward into far western PA early this afternoon. Conditions will be monitored for a possible weather watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorm development is expected in the next 1 to 2 hours. A watch is likely by mid afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 16Z surface analysis and 12Z RAOBs show a relatively homogeneous thermodynamic profile across much of the Ohio Valley and western Appalachians featuring low to mid 70s dewpoints, temperatures in the upper 80s to near 90, and mid level lapse rates around 7 C/km. SPC mesoanalysis, and a modified 12Z BUF RAOB, shows limited CINH across western New York and northwest Pennsylvania. As a result, a cumulus field has started to expand with some towering cumulus now see in visible satellite along the lake breeze off of Lake Erie. There are two areas of low-level confluence which could trigger thunderstorms in the next few hours. The first is the lake breeze along Lake Erie. Mean winds will take any storms which develop along this boundary eastward rather quickly and should support a more discrete storm mode amid supercell wind profiles. The second area of confluence is a pre-frontal trough which extends from near Wayne County, New York southward into central Pennsylvania. Storms which develop in this region will be on the eastern periphery of the best instability and as a result may build/travel southward. Storm mode could be a bit more complicated in this region, but effective shear of 40 knots (and strengthening) should be sufficient for supercells. Additionally storms are expected to develop along the cold front in Ontario/northern Ohio and eventually move into this area. Therefore, some areas could see multiple rounds of severe weather. This will likely have the greatest potential for upscale growth and greater wind damage potential into the evening. Shear has increased significantly through the morning from around 30 knots on the 12Z PIT and BUF RAOB to around 40 knots per SPC mesoanalysis. The KBUF VWP has recently sampled this strengthening flow with around 40 knots at 4k

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered thunderstorm development along the crest of the southern Appalachians should continue this afternoon. Pulse type storms may eventually result in some clustering with a risk for damaging wind gusts. A watch is possible though uncertain.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Along the eastern periphery of the TN valley/Mid South ridge of high pressure, subtle height falls/cooling aloft were supporting the development of scattered thunderstorms along the crest of the southern Appalachians. Triggered primarily by diurnally driven terrain circulations, additional storm development appears likely through the afternoon as outflow from ongoing storms interacts with the hot and unstable airmass (3000-3500 J/kg of MLCAPE). Some risk for isolated damaging winds may develop with better organized pulse like storms as downdrafts mature. Shear profiles are modest (EBWD less than 20 kt), but some enhancement of the mid-level flow along the periphery of the ridge and consolidation of outflow from ongoing storms may support additional clustering into a loosely organized MCS later this afternoon. Should this occur, a locally greater risk for damaging winds may develop given favorably large buoyancy and potential for water loaded downdrafts. While it currently appears a weather watch is not needed, convective trends will be monitored for any increase in organization/clustering this afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Continued storm development is likely through the afternoon with a threat for large hail and damaging winds.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of storms has developed over the mountains in southern Pennsylvania this morning with a few severe thunderstorm warnings issued. Satellite and radar trends show additional development in the vicinity which should also pose a threat for strong to severe storms. Effective shear is in the 25 to 30 knot range which will support multicell clusters and occasional rotating updrafts. Damaging winds and isolated large hail will be the primary threat through the afternoon, especially if any forward propagating clusters can develop. The primary limiting factor is the more stable airmass to the east, but southward moving clusters should be able to maintain themselves with moist/unstable air west of the surface trough. A severe thunderstorm watch may need to be considered if severe storms become more numerous/show greater organization.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Ongoing storms, will continue eastward with a risk for damaging wind gusts and hail. Storms with supercellular characteristics are maturing suggesting a localized greater severe potential downstream into PA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As of 1915 UTC, regional radar analysis showed scattered thunderstorms maturing ahead of a pre frontal trough/lake breeze boundary across portions of northeastern OH and northwestern PA. Supercell characteristics have emerged on two of the more dominant storms (Ashtabula/Trumbull and Wayne/Holmes counties) in OH suggesting a locally greater risk of damaging wind gusts and severe hail. While lapse rates are not particularly steep (7 C/km), 40+ kt of effective shear from the 19z PBZ special sounding should continue to support supercells capable damaging winds and potentially hail near 2 inches. Additional severe storm development will be possible farther west into central OH, though uncertainty remains higher. ..Lyons.. 06/16/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe weather threat is increasing across portions of northern and western New York.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several strong supercells have developed in Ontario and are tracking across Lake Ontario toward western/northern New York. Cooler lake temperatures are likely suppressing convective intensity somewhat at the current time. However, these storms are expected to move out of the lake shadow in the next 1 to 2 hours and more robust/severe storms are likely as a result. The wind profile continues to improve across the region as 45-55 knot mid-level flow from the 17Z BUF RAOB has now increased to 55-65 knots per BUF 19Z VWP. In addition, as these storms move east, they will encounter more backed low-level winds as they cross the pre frontal trough. The environment east of this trough continues to warm and moisten with SPC mesoanalysis now suggesting limited surface based inhibition. Therefore, an enhanced tornado threat will likely be present with any supercells in this region. One such storm which has the greatest near term tornado risk is the storm developing in Wayne county. If this storm can maintain itself east of the trough, which may occur given recent destabilization across northern New York, tornadoes will be possible. Given the backed surface flow across this region, there is significant low-level streamwise vorticity (see BGM VWP), to support this tornado threat. In addition, the lower-tropospheric winds are expected to strengthen through the afternoon as the mid-level trough approaches the region.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for damaging wind gusts should continue through this afternoon and into early this evening across WW377.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: After several hours of convective development, cold pool coalescence has taken place with multiple multi-cell clusters across the Carolinas and south-central VA. Very unstable conditions remain in place with 3500-4000 J/kg of MLCAPE owing to surface dewpoints in the low to mid 70s F. Despite limited vertical shear, radar trends and the latest hi-res guidance suggests further consolidation of storm clusters should continue into a loose MCS across the Carolinas and southern VA late this afternoon and into this evening. Isolated damaging wind gusts will remain possible with the strongest downdrafts and several reports of wind damage over the last hour lend credence to the strengthening cold pool within the cluster. Storms should continue to pose a severe wind risk as they move slowly south and southeast within WW377. ..Lyons.. 06/16/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong to severe storms continue with a threat of primarily damaging winds into the evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several strong storms have developed over the mountains and started drifting into northern Virginia and central Maryland. However, these storms have weakened rather quickly after leaving the terrain as they move into the more stable airmass closer to the coast. The airmass ahead of these storms is destabilizing and could destabilize enough for the severe weather threat to extend to at least Chesapeake Bay. Farther east, destabilization may be difficult, and a downstream severe thunderstorm watch is unlikely. A second round of storms is still expected later this evening. Therefore, watch 378 will likely remain in effect in the wake of the ongoing cluster of storms.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging winds and large hail will remain possible with a southeastward moving cluster of supercells. With shear diminishing to the south, the severe threat may become more isolated with time. Depending on trends, a new downstream watch could be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of supercell thunderstorms continues to move southeastward through southeast Ohio and into southwestern Pennsylvania. Radar imagery over the last hour or so from KPBZ shows that storm organization may be on the decrease. This is in part due to interactions between the nearby storms as well as being farther removed from the stronger mid-level winds to the north. As these storms continue into parts of West Virginia, the thermodynamic environment will remain similar while the shear, as mentioned, will continue to weaken. Given the current organization of the storms, at least some threat for damaging winds and large hail will exist into West Virginia. Depending on convective trends, this may warrant a new severe thunderstorm watch. ..Wendt.. 06/16/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A locally higher tornado threat is evident in north-central Pennsylvania with two ongoing supercells.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Two supercells are ongoing north of State College. The western cells has generally exhibited outflow-dominant characteristics on KCCX radar. The eastern cell developed recently along a stationary boundary within central Pennsylvania. While the thermodynamic environment in eastern Pennsylvania becomes less favorable, a narrow window for a locally higher tornado threat is evident given the backed surface winds in north-central Pennsylvania and consequently higher effective SRH. This threat may continue for another 1-1.5 hours or until storms ingest far less buoyant air to the east. ..Wendt.. 06/16/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated sustained thunderstorm development is possible into the 7-9 PM CDT time frame, including the evolution of occasional supercell structures posing at least some risk for large hail, locally strong surface gusts and perhaps a brief tornado. It is not clear that a severe weather watch is needed, but trends will continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At least attempts at sustained thunderstorm development are underway near a weak surface low, along a zone of stronger differential surface heating, beneath the periphery of a plume of warmer and more strongly capping elevated mixed-layer air. This is also near the northwestern periphery of prominent ridging around the 500 mb level, but veering wind profiles with height beneath weak to modest westerly 500 mb flow may be contributing to sufficient shear to promote the evolution of supercell structures. It is possible that inflow into to this storm is or will increasingly emanate from a narrow corridor characterized by 70+ F dew points along the front, which is supporting strong to extreme CAPE in excess of 3000 J/kg. If low-level convergence and weak warm advection are able to continue to overcome inhibition and maintain thunderstorm development into the 00-02Z time frame, it could become augmented by increasing shear associated with a modest strengthening southerly low-level jet (up to 30 kt around 850 mb).

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A threat for damaging winds, isolated marginally severe hail, and a brief tornado may continue in parts of central Virginia for another 1-2 hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An ongoing cluster of storms northwest of Richmond continues to slowly propagate south-southwestward into the axis of greater MLCAPE. Shear remains modest this far south, and with surface winds continuing to veer in southeast/south-central Virginia, it is not expected to improve. The large MLCAPE available will likely foster some continued threat for damaging winds/microbursts. Marginally severe hail could occur with new updrafts. KAKQ VWP data and current storm motion would suggest slightly higher SRH than noted in objective mesoanalysis. A brief tornado may occur along the southern/southwest flank of the cluster before MLCIN becomes more substantial. ..Wendt.. 06/16/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Intensifying thunderstorm development posing some risk for severe hail, and then damaging wind gusts, appears possible through 9-11 PM CDT along a corridor south of Kirksville toward the Greater St. Louis area. It is not certain a severe weather watch will be needed, but trends are being monitored for this possibility.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convective development, including isolated thunderstorms south through east-southeast of Lamoni IA, appears supported by lift associated with a zone of mid-level warm advection. This is within modest west-northwesterly flow, near the northern periphery of prominent mid-level ridging centered across parts of the southern Great Plains, Mid South and Southeast. Forcing to support convection becoming rooted within the boundary layer into this evening remains unclear, but perhaps downdrafts may eventually contribute to a surface cold pool sufficiently strong to do so. And various model output appears to suggest that this is possible. If this occurs, the boundary layer along and to the southeast of the ongoing convection is seasonably warm and characterized by high moisture content (mid 70s F dew points), which appears to be contributing to extreme CAPE in excess of 4000 J/kg. This environment may be marginally conducive to the evolution of a southeastward propagating cell, occasionally exhibiting supercell structures before growing upscale into a small, organizing cluster posing a risk for damaging wind gusts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The evolution of an organizing cluster of thunderstorms with increasing risk for potentially damaging wind gusts is possible through 11 PM-1 AM CDT. Trends are being monitored for a severe weather watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Lower/mid-tropospheric warm advection has contributed to a persistent area of thunderstorm development, near and to the west of the Omaha NE area. This is occurring on the northern periphery of the prominent mid-level ridging, within modest (25-30 kt) west-northwesterly flow around 500 mb. The convection is generally based above a cooler and much drier surface-based air mass, to the north of a remnant frontal, beneath a plume of warm elevated mixed-layer air. The warmest, and more strongly capping, air around the 700 mb level extends in west-east axis across much of Kansas into central and southern Missouri, and the convection currently across southeastern Nebraska appears likely to continue developing east-southeastward along the mid-level thermal gradient into the overnight hours. Near and shortly after 05-06Z, models suggest that the nose of a veering branch of the Great Plains low-level jet may contribute to strengthening warm advection in lower levels, where forcing for ascent and increasing inflow of seasonably high boundary-layer moisture content may contribute to substantive further upscale growth and intensification of convection. The drier low-level environment across southeastern Nebraska may already be contributing to the development of a surface cold pool, and this may continue to strengthen while spreading southeastward with the convection. Gradually, as convection continues to expand and intensify, aided by increasing inflow with large CAPE, it may become increasingly organized, with the evolution of an MCV and strengthening rear inflow which may contribute to increasing risk for strong surface gusts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for strong, potentially damaging wind gusts appears likely to increase in a corridor north through northeast of Kansas City through 1-3 AM CDT. Trends are being monitored for the possibility of an additional severe weather watch to the southeast of WW 379 within the next couple of hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A lower/mid tropospheric cyclonic circulation has become better defined within a small but intensifying cluster now approaching areas northwest through north of St. Joseph MO. 20-25 kt of south-southeasterly near-surface inflow, increasingly emanating from a boundary-layer with surface dew points in the mid/upper 70s F and characterized by extreme CAPE up to 4000+ J/kg, provides considerable potential for substantive further intensification of updrafts. And subsequent intensification of downdrafts likely will aid the downward transfer of strengthening rear inflow (in excess of 50 kt) during the next few hours. Strongest surface gusts may focus in a narrow corridor to the southwest/south of the developing MCV, which may approach northeastern portions of the Greater Kansas City area, and spread across and east-southeast of the Chillicothe vicinity through 07-09Z. ..Kerr.. 06/17/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for isolated large hail and thunderstorm winds to 60 mph will continue through the morning.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Two main areas of severe thunderstorm potential remain this morning: one across southeast Nebraska and northeast Kansas and another across northeast Missouri into central Illinois. Across southeast Nebraska and northeast Kansas, thunderstorms continue to redevelop within a warm-air advection regime. These thunderstorms are being fed within a CAPE reservoir in excess of 3000 J/kg and effective-layer shear around 30 knots. RAP point-forecast soundings indicate these storms are originating just above the 850-mb level, and tapping into mid-level lapse rates around 7 C/km. Given the elevated nature of the thunderstorms and modest lapse rates, the primary concern with these thunderstorms will be severe hail around 1-1.5 inches in diameter. The severe threat here may locally persist past the expiration of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 379, however, the localized nature of the threat should not require a new watch. To the southeast, across northeast Missouri and eventually into central Illinois, a well-organized cluster of thunderstorms continues to move east-southeast. The atmosphere along and ahead of these thunderstorms is extremely unstable, with CAPE values in excess of 4000 J/kg estimated by modified RAP soundings. However, unlike areas to the northwest, effective-layer shear is considerably less along and ahead of these thunderstorms, decreasing to less than 20 knots across central Illinois. The well-organized nature of the existing thunderstorms and the extreme instability should compensate somewhat for the weak effective-layer shear resulting in a continued severe threat for the next few hours, with the primary concern being wind gusts around 60 mph and hail around 1 inch. mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for thunderstorm winds in excess of 60 mph will continue this morning. A new watch will likely be needed across portions of southern Illinois, southeast Missouri, western Kentucky, and southwest Indiana.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A well-organized mesoscale convective system continues moving east-southeast this morning into a strongly unstable environment. Although effective-layer shear remains poor, storm- and mesoscale organization will combine with the unstable environment to pose a continued threat of thunderstorm winds in excess of 60 miles per hour. As such a new Severe Thunderstorm Watch downstream of watch #380 will likely be required this morning.
